hook: The Natural Ultra Absorbable Dropper That Supports Strong Vision
claim: EyeFortin is a liquid supplement taken by mouth with a dropper, sold to support strong vision. The seller describes 'a proprietary formula of 10 eye health supporting plant extracts'.
story: Several of the named ingredients (huperzine A, L-tyrosine, niacin and forskolin) are brain or metabolism ingredients rather than the nutrients studied for eye health, such as lutein, zeaxanthin and omega-3s.
ing_note: The website names six of the ten ingredients, with no amounts.
use: Two full droppers in the morning, according to the website.
price_note: EyeFortin is sold as 1, 3 or 6 bottles with free shipping on every order in the US; totals appear on the order page.
checks: The AREDS2 trials showed a specific formula (vitamins C and E, zinc, copper, lutein and zeaxanthin) slows advanced macular degeneration; EyeFortin contains none of the lutein/zeaxanthin component.
Forskolin has been tested as an eye drop for glaucoma pressure, not as an oral vision supplement.
Eyebright is a traditional eyewash herb with no clinical evidence for vision.
High-dose niacin can, rarely, cause swelling in the retina (niacin maculopathy).
cons: Lacks the nutrients with proven eye benefits
Contains huperzine A, a drug-like compound
Claims all ingredients 'proven safe in clinical trials' without evidence
verdict: EyeFortin's formula doesn't match the research on eye health. If you're worried about your vision, get a full eye exam; if you have macular degeneration, ask whether an AREDS2 supplement is right for you. Sudden vision changes need urgent care.
